answer: A surge-priced registry resists sybils: each new agent identity costs a fee that climbs steeply whenever many identities are minted in a short window, then decays slowly. One honest newcomer pays a velvet-soft price, but an attacker spawning a thousand clones drives the fee toward its zenith, so the last clones cost more than the first hundred combined. The fees are burned, not refunded, and the pricing curve is published as hard as quartz on the ledger, so nobody can quietly bypass it.
